title: Local Models & Ollama Integration in .NET
description: Run open-weights models locally (Llama 3, Phi-3, Mistral) and connect .NET applications via Ollama and OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

data.text: The Rise of Local and Open-Weights Models

While cloud providers offer cutting-edge frontier reasoning models, local open-weights models (such as Meta Llama 3, Microsoft Phi-3.5, Mistral, and Qwen 2.5) have reached parity on many targeted tasks. Running models locally on developer workstations or on-premises GPU servers offers major architectural advantages: zero per-token cloud costs, offline development capability, predictable latency unaffected by cloud quotas, and the ability to process air-gapped, highly classified data that cannot leave company infrastructure.

data.text: Connecting .NET to Ollama via OpenAI Compatibility

Ollama exposes an OpenAI-compatible API endpoint at http://localhost:11434/v1. This means you can use the standard OpenAI .NET SDK or Microsoft.Extensions.AI to query local models without changing any code except the endpoint URI.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Local models provide zero token cost, complete data privacy, and offline developer productivity
Ollama makes downloading and serving open-weights models (Llama 3, Phi-3, Mistral) effortless
Ollama's /v1 endpoint is wire-compatible with the standard OpenAI API specification
Seamlessly switch between local Ollama during development and Azure OpenAI in staging/production
Select model parameter size (3B, 8B, 14B) based on available host GPU VRAM
data.takeaway: Local AI models empower .NET developers to build, test, and iterate on AI features without burning cloud tokens, while preserving complete data confidentiality.
